summary_paragraph: A woman with idiopathic chronic pancreatitis was admitted with a five-day history of epigastric pain radiating to the back and nonbloody emesis, consistent with an acute exacerbation. She was managed with bowel rest, TPN infusion via her existing PICC line, and symptom control using IV hydromorphone and ondansetron. Her pain and nausea gradually improved, allowing transition to oral medications and a soft diet by hospital day 6. She was started on oral vitamin B12 due to borderline low levels, and impacted cerumen was identified in the right ear, with instructions to avoid self-cleaning and follow up with her PCP or ENT. She was discharged home in stable condition with plans for close GI follow-up to manage TPN discontinuation, nutritional lab monitoring, and iron supplementation as an outpatient.
